skill.name: animejs
skill.description: Guides agents in writing deterministic Anime.js animations inside HyperFrames compositions, including timeline setup, adapter registration, and render-safe validation.
skill.summary: Build seek-driven Anime.js animations for HyperFrames compositions.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: The markdown backtick and system reconnaissance detections are false positives caused by documentation formatting and defensive guidance. Two CDN examples are confirmed low-severity network dependencies because copied compositions would load Anime.js from jsDelivr.

remediation.issue: Examples load Anime.js from a public CDN.
remediation.suggestion: Offer a local package import or pinned vendored asset option for offline and reproducible renders.

remediation.issue: Validation commands are shown without installation context.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that authors should run HyperFrames validation in a trusted project with reviewed dependencies.

static_findings.snippet: HyperFrames can seek Anime.js instances through its `animejs` runtime adapter. The composition owns
- Set `autoplay: false` so Anime.js does not advance on its own clock.
- Register every returned animation or timeline on `window.__hfAnime`.
The adapter seeks every registered instance with `instance.seek(timeMs)`, where `timeMs` is HyperFra
If you use an ES module build, the adapter does not care how the instance was created. It only needs
- Depending on `anime.running` auto-discovery instead of explicit `window.__hfAnime.push(...)`.
- Avoid callbacks that mutate DOM based on wall-clock time, network state, or unseeded randomness.

content.value_statement: HyperFrames renders need deterministic animation timing. This skill shows how to register Anime.js animations for seek-driven playback.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to register Anime.js instances on window.__hfAnime.
Shows basic animation and timeline patterns for HyperFrames compositions.
Guides authors to disable autoplay for deterministic seeking.
Describes ES module usage when the instance exposes seek and pause methods.
Lists validation commands for HyperFrames linting and composition checks.
limitations: It does not provide a full Anime.js API reference.
It does not replace GSAP for complex HyperFrames scene sequencing.
It assumes the composition already includes valid HyperFrames structure.
CDN examples require network access unless adapted to local dependencies.

use_cases.title: Add Small DOM Motion
use_cases.description: Use Anime.js syntax for simple marks, labels, chips, and SVG flourishes inside a render-safe composition.

use_cases.title: Convert Existing Examples
use_cases.description: Translate an Anime.js example into a HyperFrames pattern with autoplay disabled and explicit adapter registration.

use_cases.title: Validate Animation Timing
use_cases.description: Check that timelines use finite durations and can be controlled by HyperFrames time instead of wall-clock playback.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Basic Animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a HyperFrames composition that animates one element with Anime.js. Disable autoplay and register the animation on window.__hfAnime.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Timeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Add an Anime.js timeline for title and accent elements. Use finite durations and make the timeline seek-driven for HyperFrames.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt Module Usage
prompt_templates.scenario: Use an ES module import pattern.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this Anime.js module example for HyperFrames. Ensure the returned instance supports seek and is pushed into window.__hfAnime.

prompt_templates.title: Review Render Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this HyperFrames composition for Anime.js render safety. Identify autoplay, infinite loops, timers, async setup, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A request to animate a logo mark across the screen with Anime.js.
output_examples.output: A HyperFrames-ready plan that disables autoplay, registers the animation, uses a finite duration, and recommends validation.

output_examples.input: An Anime.js timeline copied from a browser demo.
output_examples.output: A revised timeline approach that uses explicit registration and avoids wall-clock callbacks or async animation creation.

output_examples.input: A composition that behaves differently between preview and render.
output_examples.output: A checklist of nondeterministic causes, including autoplay, timers, network state, random values, and missing HyperFrames validation.

best_practices: Create animations synchronously during composition initialization.
Disable autoplay and let HyperFrames control time through seeking.
Use finite durations and loop counts for reproducible renders.
anti_patterns: Do not depend on Anime.js automatic running animation discovery.
Do not create animations after timers, promises, event handlers, or async asset loads.
Do not use infinite loops when a finite repeat count can match the composition duration.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Anime.js animations that HyperFrames can seek during deterministic rendering.

faq.question: Does it require Anime.js autoplay?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends disabling autoplay so HyperFrames controls animation time.

faq.question: Can it use Anime.js timelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to create a timeline and register it with the HyperFrames adapter.

faq.question: Does it support ES module builds?
faq.answer: Yes. The instance must expose seek and pause methods before registration.

faq.question: When should authors use GSAP instead?
faq.answer: Authors should use GSAP for complex scene sequencing unless Anime.js is specifically required.

faq.question: What should authors validate after changes?
faq.answer: Authors should run HyperFrames linting and validation in a trusted project environment.
